subject: Request: Temporary SLO reprofiling during Lumos data migration
messages:
From: Amaya Rao <amaya@lumos.ai>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, ops@datamigrate.io
Cc: sre@lumos.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Temporary SLO reprofiling during Lumos data migration

Hi Avery,

Quick context: Lumos is doing a user-data consolidation/migration next week (large historical payloads being backfilled into our product). During our internal load testing we saw sustained p95 spikes for hosted inference calls during prefix-heavy batches. We want to request a temporary, limited reprofiling of the hosted API latency SLOs for the migration window so our rollout doesn't get throttled/fail the SLA gates.

Requested reprofiling window and targets:
- Window: 2028-04-07 02:00 UTC -> 2028-04-08 14:00 UTC (36 hours)
- Proposed p50: 120 ms (current committed: 80 ms)
- Proposed p95: 500 ms (current committed: 300 ms)
- Measurement: keep existing p50/p95 quantile calculation, but allow a regional carveout for east-us traffic originating from Lumos IP ranges.

We plan to run migration traffic in batches with an SRE canary prior to full migration. We can accept additional operational guardrails from Redwood (e.g., reduced burst capacity, request-level throttles, and a hard abort on error-rate regressions).

Attached is our migration plan (lumos-migration-plan.pdf) and a small sample of telemetry that demonstrates the expected tail behavior.

Can you advise on what formality is required for this exception (legal amendment, temporary addendum, or an operational exception note), and whether Redwood can commit to: 1) accepting this temporary reprofiling for the stated window, and 2) providing a canary + rollback playbook with telemetry hooks to make the migration safe?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

— Amaya
Amaya Rao
Head of Platform Engineering, Lumos AI
amaya@lumos.ai
+1 415-555-0189
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Amaya Rao <amaya@lumos.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 2 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary SLO reprofiling during Lumos data migration

Amaya — thanks for the clear ask and the migration plan. I read the attached telemetry sample and the pattern you described tracks with what we see for prefix-heavy backfills. We can support a temporary reprofiling but want to narrow the window and lock down the operational controls so this doesn't create broader customer noise.

Proposed Redwood controls and countermeasures:
- Narrower active window: allow a max of 24 hours of the higher p95 (we recommend 2028-04-07 02:00 UTC -> 2028-04-07 26:00 UTC / effectively 2028-04-08 02:00 UTC). If you need an extension we require a formal post-mortem and approval.
- Canary: a staged canary for the first 2 migration batches with explicit SLO gates (error-rate < 0.5%, p95 within 120% of baseline for the canary population).
- Traffic shaping: we will apply per-API-key rate caps and a temporary lower burst token allocation for the migration API key.
- Cache warmup: we can coordinate a KV-cache warmup run with you prior to the canary to reduce tail events.
- Fallback model variant: we can route to a slightly smaller model variant with identical output surface for traffic over the threshold; Redwood will log when fallback occurs.
- Measurement windowing: maintain standard quantile computation but isolate the Lumos-origin traffic by IP/DST so the reprofiling does not affect other customers' SLOs.

Operational asks from Lumos:
1) Provide a definitive list of source IP blocks for the carveout.
2) Share a short rollback playbook for us to execute if error-rate or hallucination metrics degrade.
3) Confirm that the migration batches will be rate-limited on your end to the numbers in the migration plan.

If you agree I will open an internal exception request and route to Rishi (SRE escalation) and Lauren (Customer Success/contracting) to align on telemetry and the amendment language. Legal may want a 1-page addendum capturing the exact window and guardrails.

I cc'ed Rishi, Lauren and Kimberly for operational sign-off.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Director, Customer Reliability 
Redwood Inference
avery_johnson@redwood.ai
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Approval request: temporary SLO reprofiling for Lumos (DEAL-2028-0149)

Team — forwarding Lumos' migration ask and proposing we grant a conditional temporary reprofiling. Key points and proposed approval conditions below. Please reply with Approve / Approve with edits / Deny. If approved, I'll draft the 1-page amendment and the operational runbook link.

Summary: Lumos requests a 36-hour window; Redwood recommends approving up to 24 hours with the following conditions.

Approval conditions (proposed):
- Window: 2028-04-07 02:00 UTC -> 2028-04-08 02:00 UTC (24 hours).
- Quantile targets during window: p50 <= 120 ms, p95 <= 500 ms. Logging of any fallback model routing required.
- Canary: first two batches must pass canary criteria (error-rate < 0.5% and p95 <= 120% of pre-migration baseline for canary subset).
- Telemetry: Lumos to provide source IP blocks, expected TPS per batch, and a small telemetry sample (they already attached a sample).
- Abort criteria: automatic abort if API error-rate exceeds 1% for 5 consecutive minutes OR if hallucination score on validation prompts rises by > 15% vs baseline.
- Post-event: Lumos will deliver a post-mortem within 72 hours if extension requested.

Related artifacts: proposed-exception-amendment.docx (attached), hubspot: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/DEAL-2028-0149, runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/pm/runbooks/lumos-migration-runbook

If we approve, legal (Kimberly) — please confirm if we need a signed amendment or if an email-confirmed operational exception is sufficient for billing/contracting. Lauren — we will need CS to coordinate the canary window with the Lumos SREs and to verify rollback readiness. Rishi — we will need SRE to own the telemetry gates and the abort automation.

Attaching a draft amendment for review.

— Avery
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 3 Apr 2028 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Approval request: temporary SLO reprofiling for Lumos (DEAL-2028-0149)

Approve with minor edits — I agree to the 24 hour cap and the canary requirements. A few edits to the abort criteria and telemetry:

- Abort criteria: change to automatic abort if API error-rate exceeds 0.8% for 3 consecutive minutes OR if hallucination score on the agreed validation set rises by > 12% vs baseline.
- Telemetry: we need a rolling 1-minute resolution feed of p50/p95 for the canary population and a separate stream for fallback events (model-id, reason code). Lumos to expose a webhook or a shared S3 bucket with the canary metrics.
- Post-event: require Lumos to attach the migration telemetry CSV and a short PTR (post-traffic report) to the HubSpot deal within 48 hours if they request any extension.

Once Kimberly confirms the amendment formality, I'm happy to own the automation for abort-triggering and fallback logging.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
